reason: AU1 first-clear acquired decks cleared C in 4/4 progress-first cases and 0/4 side-first cases. Distinguish a rigid target-order problem from a blanket stat imbalance before changing content durability.
checkpoints: Recreate the four AU1 first-clear checkpoints at offsets 0/8 via A/B using the identical natural tags, equipment, deck policy and next seed; no purchases or extra grants are needed at the first return.
runs: Four checkpoint reconstruction runs plus eight C forks: initial/use-owned with one new public-state policy. The original sixteen C progress/side runs are read from AU1 results, not rerun or retuned.
policy: Start from AH progress_first, including its current healing and guard rules.

When its choice is an attack, keep a goal that can be completed immediately. Otherwise allow a support target to interrupt only when a visible prediction completes it now; order such candidates by action cost then card ID.

For placement only, among non-healing placements with the same remaining lifetime as the default choice, prefer lower field power + field hit/10 if a visible active enemy acts before the player's next action. Do not inspect enemy hands or future draw/order. This potential-material score is a heuristic, not an expected damage forecast.
limits: Follow-up defined after AU1 to diagnose a specific observed contrast. Not an independent holdout or a globally optimal policy.
Same content HP, concealment, deck, passive capacity and reward rules. Record all outcomes, including deterioration, with exact paired labels.
The new policy changes target and placement heuristics together; aggregate results do not isolate the causal contribution of either one. Changes are counted separately.
